public_payload.normalized_proposition: The generative AI boom will fall apart, leading to a very public reckoning for the tech industry.

statement.excerpt: And when this all falls apart — and I believe it will — there will be a very public reckoning for the tech industry.

our_interpretation: This is a joint prediction that the generative AI boom will collapse and that its collapse will produce a prominent public reckoning.
The explicit assertion that it will fall apart makes collapse part of the prediction, rather than an external antecedent whose absence makes the whole claim unscorable.

The plain reading of falls apart is a broad, sustained breakdown of the boom, evidenced across financing, valuations, investment activity, or major business failures. A single failed company or market correction is insufficient.
A very public reckoning means prominent accountability proceedings or sustained industry-wide scrutiny explicitly responding to that breakdown. It need not result in criminal convictions.
No deadline or required lag between collapse and reckoning is stated.
criteria.support_condition: A documented broad collapse of the generative AI boom is followed by prominent public accountability proceedings or sustained scrutiny of the tech industry explicitly tied to that collapse.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A clearly completed collapse and aftermath establish that the asserted public reckoning did not occur. Continued growth, an isolated setback, or the absence of proceedings by an arbitrary date cannot contradict this undated prediction.

evidence.excerpt: While overall venture investment remains robust, the market is becoming increasingly concentrated around a relatively small number of large AI-related funding rounds.
evidence.locator: Paragraph preceding AI megadeals continue to dominate venture funding
evidence.explanation: KPMG's quarterly research describes continued investment alongside concentration, which cautions against declaring a broad collapse established. It covers a wider venture market and cannot rule out a future generative AI collapse.

evidence.publisher: Office of U.S. Senator Josh Hawley
evidence.explanation: This official press release establishes prominent public demands for accountability concerning alleged AI cyberattacks. It does not establish a collapse of the generative AI boom or scrutiny caused by such a collapse.
